key_insight: REFLEX uses a fast typed decision layer (Jev) to route only uncertain or generative cases to a strong LLM, cutting compute while preserving task success.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical control pattern for LLM agents: use cheap deterministic routing for bounded actions and reserve expensive model calls for low-confidence decisions.
method: Jev handles fast, typed action selection for bounded decisions.
A strong LLM is called only when confidence is low or generation is required.
The approach is tested against fallback families and external benchmarks.
evidence_signal: On a frozen 100-task benchmark, REFLEX reaches 95% success while making 72.7% fewer strong-model calls than a strong-only agent.
watch_item: Benefits may be limited when ordinary routing is already highly accurate, especially on external BFCL and τ-style evaluations.
paper_title: REFLEX with Jev for Efficient Selective Control in LLM Agents
